claim: Multiplying zeta by its pole- and gamma-correcting factors, folding with the functional equation, and then writing s=1/2+it preserves the nontrivial-zero question while replacing a meromorphic strip problem by an entire even function whose critical-line zeros are real t-roots.
historical_or_program_relation: Riemann's theta-integral split-reflect-center construction, the later explicit separation of xi zeros from gamma/pole artifacts, and the modern real-rootedness formulation are successive presentations of the same representation change and its preserved zero data.
limits: Completion proves symmetry, decay, and confinement only after analytic continuation, Euler-product nonvanishing, and the functional equation are available; evenness and reality on the line do not imply that all zeros are real or even supply an existence proof.
title: Completion and recentering isolate the nontrivial zero geometry

claim: Logarithms and transforms turn the Euler product into an additive prime-power count, residues turn analytic singularities into a zero expansion, and Mobius inversion removes prime-power iterates only at the later prime-counting stage; because the zero expansion is conditionally convergent, contour-induced magnitude ordering is part of the representation.
historical_or_program_relation: Riemann's ordered zero sum and Mobius separation are made explicit in modern prime-zero duality accounts, which retain the weighted prime-power density as the directly reconstructible intermediate object before optionally recovering primes alone.
limits: The bridge does not make arbitrary rearrangements valid, and a finite or smoothed zero sum recovers only a resolution-limited approximation; treating prime powers as removable noise before inversion discards signal that the explicit formula naturally preserves.
title: The prime-zero bridge retains prime powers and a summation prescription

claim: A vertical Perron kernel converts a Dirichlet series into cumulative coefficients through residues, but a valid finite contour requires both a remainder representation with edge decay and a height budget whose truncation error grows near the cutoff discontinuity.
historical_or_program_relation: The generalized-series proof isolates decay by subtracting the pre-cutoff terms and shifting by the first surviving exponent, while the modern truncated formula exposes contour height as a frequency-resolution parameter; both refine the general Dirichlet-series-to-summatory-function bridge.
limits: The line must remain to the right of the relevant convergence boundary, the sharp cutoff has a canonical half-weight at equality, and neither the abstract inversion template nor larger height alone controls a raw remainder whose horizontal edges fail to vanish.
title: Perron inversion trades sharp coefficient recovery for decay and resolution obligations

claim: A finite-height RH certificate is obtained by matching an argument-principle total zero count to critical-line sign-change witnesses after phase normalization, while absolute error envelopes, endpoint closure, count identities, reruns, and overlapping computations protect the numerical-to-integer step.
historical_or_program_relation: The conceptual count-plus-witness certificate is refined by computational practice from Gram-point detection into explicit truncation/interpolation/arithmetic error margins and targeted reruns of known bookkeeping vulnerabilities.
limits: Gram-point sampling is not itself complete, adjacent-block recovery has a documented counterexample pattern, related program versions and machines are not independent implementations, and the conclusion is only for the certified finite rectangle.
title: Finite RH verification composes exhaustive counts with certified line witnesses

claim: Finite zero verification can anchor the low-height side of an all-height zero-free inequality, while an asymptotic zero-free region controls the upper side; contour height then balances inversion error against allowable displacement to transfer the joined coverage into explicit psi, theta, and prime-counting errors.
historical_or_program_relation: The qualitative PNT contour mechanism is converted into an explicit coverage-and-optimization pipeline in which verified height, zero-free geometry, finite psi estimates, and downstream reoptimization are separate improvement levers.
limits: The splice inherits every constant, crossover, and overlap obligation of its inputs; verified RH below a height says nothing by itself above it, the levers are not interchangeable, and the resulting error remains far from the square-root scale that full RH would imply.
title: Verified zeros and zero-free geometry cover complementary ranges in explicit prime bounds

claim: Kernel smoothing and Mellin transformation replace a conditionally organized zero formula by weighted identities that permit interchange, integration, factorization, tail bounds, and transfer across weight families; this can let one low zero pair force oscillation after the remaining weighted tail is controlled.
historical_or_program_relation: The contour-prescribed ordering already present in Riemann's formula becomes an explicit regularization technology in smoothed explicit formulas and transform-Tauberian arguments, relocating the burden from formal summation to kernel choice and endpoint estimates.
limits: A smoothed oscillation result is not automatically a statement about the raw summatory error, unsmoothing requires Tauberian hypotheses, and changing the kernel or ordering changes the admissible manipulations and the quantitative tail rather than merely changing notation.
title: Smoothing makes zero expansions operable but changes the recovery problem

claim: Zero statistics and involutive eigenvalue pairing motivate a spectral formulation but do not supply spectral reality; a credible Hilbert-Polya mechanism must construct a zero-independent space and a legitimate common domain or geometric sign structure from which the zeros and their reality follow.
historical_or_program_relation: Random-matrix and finite-field analogies state the structural target, Connes's cokernel/support mechanism shows how zeros can emerge where an analytic multiplier fails to force density, and the proposed difference Hamiltonian exposes domain, adjoint, completeness, and self-adjointness as the unresolved decisive obligations.
limits: Connes's support classification and the formal Hamiltonian are distinct constructions and cannot be fused into one operator; PT symmetry only pairs eigenvalues, the cited statistics are motivational, and neither program as represented here proves self-adjointness or RH.
title: A spectral model must derive rather than encode the zeros

claim: Random-matrix characteristic polynomials can match local correlations, lower-order extreme-value behavior, and moment predictions while omitting Euler-product arithmetic; the hybrid Euler-Hadamard representation repairs that loss by assigning prime data and nearby-zero data to compensating factors whose product is stable as the cutoff changes.
historical_or_program_relation: Agreement of independently motivated moment heuristics and numerical freezing diagnostics strengthens a universality program, while the later hybrid factorization turns the known arithmetic mismatch into an explicit two-factor representation rather than an external correction constant alone.
limits: The moment agreements and freezing curve are heuristic or numerical and have slow finite-height convergence; the hybrid split is cutoff-dependent, its compensating plots are representation checks, and neither universality evidence nor factorization establishes RH or an underlying self-adjoint operator.
title: Universal zero statistics require a separate arithmetic factor

claim: Embedding zeta in a larger theory can expose missing geometry, automorphy, or Hecke structure, but a componentwise bicomplex lift transports continuation and zero data through two scalar projections without adding such a mechanism; its conjunctive zero set is a Cartesian pairing, and a hyperbolic restriction collapses the nontrivial zero geometry.
historical_or_program_relation: The general L-function program uses enlargement to seek shared arithmetic or spectral invariants, whereas the bicomplex construction is a controlled counterexample to treating every formally broader zeta object as an explanatory generalization.
limits: The bicomplex continuation and reconstruction are legitimate representation transfers and are not refuted by this comparison; the point is only that component independence and zero divisors add no demonstrated route to classical RH, while membership in the broader automorphic or geometric L-function package remains difficult in its own right.
title: Generalization is informative only when it exposes a new invariant

claim: To make a family of L-functions close under reflection, one must split sign and conductor classes, attach parity-dependent gamma factors, correct imprimitive twists so dual summation orders agree, and then use a uniformly controlled Mobius sieve to recover the primitive family.
historical_or_program_relation: This realizes the general-L-function idea that a shared analytic package comes from arithmetic structure: completion advances from a single-function involution to a finite-dimensional system of commuting family involutions, with correction polynomials and sieving carrying the new proof burden.
limits: The initial completed family symmetry does not by itself continue to the averaging pole or prove a moment theorem; correction uniqueness is limited to the stated low degrees, bad-prime formulas remain essential, and formal Mobius cancellation without uniform bounds cannot transfer continuation.
title: Family functional equations require completion of both local factors and the index set

claim: An explicit formula can turn inaccessible zero information into a quadratic sign obligation or a residual term, and kernel design determines which arithmetic data are emphasized; demanding one sign for every admissible test function is categorically stronger than tuning a kernel to known small prime ideals for a finite explicit bound.
historical_or_program_relation: The RH positivity/negativity criterion presents test functions as a uniform structural probe modeled on geometric intersection signs, while discriminant computations use local arithmetic knowledge to choose data-adaptive kernels and infer an otherwise inaccessible zero contribution by subtraction.
limits: A successful data-tuned kernel does not establish uniform negativity, and the finite-field intersection sign does not identify or prove the missing classical quadratic representation; residual computation is valid only with fixed identity and kernel conventions.
title: Explicit-formula kernels separate uniform sign criteria from data-tuned certification

claim: Theta-transform representations convert completed-zeta derivatives into moments: one route amplifies an eventual sign of Xi into rigid derivative signs, while another packages central Taylor coefficients into Jensen polynomials whose hyperbolicity tests finite coefficient windows and whose eventual behavior follows from uniform saddle-point ratio asymptotics.
historical_or_program_relation: The classical Fourier/moment sign-change strategy and the modern Jensen-polynomial criterion use the same positive-moment access to completed-zeta coefficients but apply different finite-dimensional probes to the zero problem.
limits: The recovered classical span stops before its intended contradiction, and eventual Jensen hyperbolicity at each fixed degree is weaker than hyperbolicity for every degree and shift required by the RH equivalence; pointwise coefficient asymptotics without uniform local ratio control are insufficient.
title: Theta moments re-encode zero geometry as coefficient geometry

claim: Prime squares can be a lower-order error in a height-averaged zeta tail, a positive mean shift in a quadratic character family, and the natural signal in a prime-power density reconstructed from zeros; whether they may be removed is therefore determined by the averaging and target representation, not by exponent alone.
historical_or_program_relation: Moment methods use time or character orthogonality to decide which prime powers survive on the diagonal, while explicit-formula reconstruction deliberately stops before Mobius inversion so that the directly produced prime-power signal is retained.
limits: The negligibility statement uses its stated RH-dependent estimates, the quadratic-family shift uses a different averaging ensemble, and neither conclusion transfers unchanged to raw prime counts or to other symmetry families.
title: Prime powers change status when the averaging symmetry changes

claim: Zeta mean-value arguments separate multiplicative equality into a residue or Ramanujan-type main term, while unequal products are reindexed by differences and then converted through Poisson/Voronoi, Vaughan-Kloosterman, or automorphic spectral transforms into structures with usable cancellation.
historical_or_program_relation: The mollified second-moment analysis uses scale-adapted bilinear Kloosterman estimates, the mean-square formula uses an analytically continued difference-indexed series, and the fourth moment replaces one-dimensional transforms by an SL(2,Z) spectral decomposition whose Maass channel survives the final asymptotic scale selection.
limits: No single off-diagonal estimate covers every range, isolating a main term does not bound the remainders, and these smoothed moment mechanisms do not directly locate individual zeta zeros or prove RH.
title: Moment proofs isolate a factorable diagonal and transform the off diagonal

claim: Introducing several complex variables creates a safe convergence domain in which an identity and its functional symmetries can be built; explicit residue extraction then continues the aggregate object, after which one may specialize to a fourth moment or read a family mean from a pole.
historical_or_program_relation: The four-variable fourth-moment formula and corrected multiple Dirichlet series share an order-of-operations discipline: regularize first, continue the whole coupled representation, and only then approach the singular target where separately divergent pieces can cancel.
limits: The fourth-moment identity and the family-moment program are different objects; in the latter, reaching and controlling the averaging pole plus Tauberian hypotheses remain genuine burdens, and a formal specialization before continuation is not licensed by aggregate cancellation.
title: Auxiliary variables make singular cancellation visible before specialization

claim: After zeta is reduced to short exponential sums, useful cancellation requires explicit interface changes: Taylor polynomialization and mean-value duplication, periodic domain enlargement for decoupling, bilinear-to-linear interval recursion, Weyl shift correlations, scale-adapted blocks, and Abel summation back to the weighted Dirichlet polynomial.
historical_or_program_relation: Classical derivative and Weyl-differencing estimates, Vinogradov mean-value assembly, and modern decoupling improve different bottlenecks in the same reduction chain; parameter and range splicing record where each adapter is quantitatively compatible with the zeta application.
limits: The methods have different hypotheses and dominant ranges and cannot be combined by retaining only their best exponents; local cancellation bounds still require weighted transfer and global contour steps, and the resulting zero-free or zeta bounds remain weaker than RH.
title: Short zeta-sum bounds depend on adapters between theorem and application geometry

claim: Iterated-logarithmic growth, zero-driven oscillations, and ill-conditioned finite truncations give three mechanisms by which a correct asymptotic or pointwise limit can remain invisible or look qualitatively false throughout feasible computation.
historical_or_program_relation: The eventual reversal of a long-observed prime-counting bias supplies an arithmetic example, while slowly diverging model functions and a q-zeta approximation near a zero show the broader mismatch between theorem-scale convergence and finite numerical behavior.
limits: These examples do not locate the first prime-bias reversal, prove typical dominance at all large scales, give a general condition number for q-zeta truncations, or license skepticism about a finite computation that has an independent rigorous error certificate.
title: Slow asymptotics make persistent finite behavior an unreliable guide

claim: The argument principle can support a finite exhaustive RH certificate by comparing a total count with line witnesses, or an asymptotic lower proportion by replacing direct line zeros with zeros of a mollified differential combination and then bounding that auxiliary count through a mean square optimized variationally.
historical_or_program_relation: The same contour-counting resource moves from computational cardinality matching to Levinson-Conrey's analytic reduction, where representation freedom in the mollifier and differential combination trades individual certification for an optimizable global proportion.
limits: The two conclusions are not interchangeable: the mollified chain uses auxiliary zeros, shifted contours, and differing multiplicity conventions, its variational optimizer must be returned to the admissible polynomial class, and a positive proportion is neither finite completeness nor RH.
title: Contour zero counts serve different goals after the auxiliary object changes

claim: Parity restrictions can be engineered before evaluation: real and imaginary parts of a contour representation select different parity-indexed log-sine moments, while a symmetric rational function makes partial fractions and integer summation produce linear forms supported only on odd zeta values.
historical_or_program_relation: Integral identities and irrationality constructions use different auxiliary objects but share a representation-level projection move that replaces accidental cancellation at the end with symmetry-controlled support from the start.
limits: The damaged integral formulas support only the proof architecture, not coefficient-level identities or a single verified projector common to the even and odd cases; the rational-function construction additionally needs denominator control and analytic smallness, and neither special-value mechanism bears directly on RH zero location.
title: Symmetry can project zeta-value identities onto parity-restricted families

claim: Finite-height RH verification is a composition of logically different certificates: a global count of all zeros in the region and enough sign-change witnesses for zeros of a real critical-line function. Extending and overlapping intervals or independently rerunning computations audits the numerical realization, but the decisive mathematical closure remains equality between exhaustive count and located witnesses.
historical_or_program_relation: Bombieri states the abstract argument-principle/count-versus-sign-change architecture; the early and large-scale computations instantiate it with Backlund/Turing-style counts, Gram-block searches, overlapping extensions, and independent reruns.
limits: The conclusion is restricted to the certified height and hypotheses of the count; sign changes alone can miss even-multiplicity zeros, while a zero count alone gives no critical-line location. Repeated agreement audits implementation but neither proves RH beyond the range nor replaces rigorous error control.
title: Exhaustive zero counts close critical-line sign searches

claim: When the theorem asks only whether a required number of roots exists, computation can retain the decision statistic and discard root coordinates: zeta verification counts certified sign changes without zooming in on ordinates, while the Jensen-polynomial method uses a Sturm sequence to count real roots rather than approximate every complex root.
historical_or_program_relation: Both programs replace high-precision root databases with completeness-oriented counts, trading reconstructive output for the exact invariant needed by the downstream theorem and thereby reducing storage or polynomial-root work.
limits: The counted objects and algorithms are different, so neither procedure transfers directly to the other. Zeta sign counts require an independent global zero-count closure, and the Jensen argument requires coefficient accuracy, a root-containing interval, and conditions under which the Sturm count is valid; count-only output cannot answer later questions about individual root locations.
title: Count-only certificates avoid unnecessary root reconstruction

claim: A bounded-error first pass can certify most signs or root counts and route only unresolved cases to a stronger formula or higher precision. In zeta computations the comparison of an approximation with its explicit remainder flags doubtful Gram points; in the Jensen computation anomalous Sturm counts trigger increased precision until sign stability and a global root interval restore completeness.
historical_or_program_relation: The early screening/fallback strategy and later interval or multiprecision implementations share a certificate architecture in which uncertainty is explicit control flow rather than silently rounded evidence.
limits: The error bounds, fallback formulas, and instability diagnostics are method-specific, and an ambiguous first pass is not evidence of a zero or counterexample. Adaptive escalation does not remove the need to prove that the final search interval is exhaustive or that every accepted sign is separated from its error bound.
title: Rigorous error bounds turn precision into an adaptive resource

claim: Global positive contributions can be certified without enumerating their full domain by splitting them into a precisely computed local part and analytically controlled exterior or tail pieces. A Lehmer-pair certificate bounds the local window from neighboring gaps and closes several upward-rounded contributions; the zero-free-region calculation substitutes verified low-zero data for a generic counting error and splits a peaked gamma integral into regions with separate rigorous bounds.
historical_or_program_relation: Across two explicit-constant programs, sharper computation enters exactly where a uniform estimate is wasteful, while monotonicity, zero-count bounds, and tail integrals retain global coverage.
limits: The summed quantities, kernels, constants, and target theorems differ, so the numerical bounds cannot be transported between programs. A local-data improvement is valid only with a proved tail decomposition and directed rounding; it does not certify omitted zeros or justify choosing the split after inspecting an unprotected target result.
title: Local computation plus analytic tails certifies global sums

claim: The raw smallness of a consecutive zero gap is not itself a de Bruijn–Newman certificate: it must be normalized by an interaction sum over the other zeros, with local zeros computed accurately and the remainder bounded, before the pair yields a lower bound for Lambda. The resulting bound is often dominated by the squared gap, explaining why extended zero searches can improve it even when the interaction estimate is coarse.
historical_or_program_relation: The first program turns a spectacular gap discovered in a broad verification run into an auditable Lehmer-pair certificate; the later analysis exposes the bound's gap-dominated sensitivity and motivates continued computation as a targeted search for stronger phase-boundary witnesses.
limits: A finite certified pair gives only a lower bound for Lambda, not RH or Lambda=0, and a search that finds no better pair is not exhaustive evidence that none exists. Gap dominance does not permit dropping the interaction sum, consecutiveness, simplicity, or tail bounds; the conditional infinite-pair limit requires an actual family with bounds tending to zero.
title: A close gap becomes a phase-boundary witness only after global normalization

claim: Finite Gram-block counts reveal stable-looking but unexplained spacing patterns; the de Bruijn–Newman program replaces a missing static probability law with a deterministic inverse-distance zero flow. A renormalized Hamiltonian dissipation argument shows that the assumption Lambda<0 would relax high zeros toward a local lattice, which is incompatible with a positive proportion of sub-mean zeta gaps.
historical_or_program_relation: Large computations posed an empirical distribution problem without a mechanism, while the later heat-flow proof uses spacing data as the terminal falsifier of a concrete dynamical consequence rather than as freestanding numerical support for RH.
limits: The heat-flow argument does not derive the observed Gram-block type distributions or supply their unknown probability law, and Gram blocks are not identical to normalized consecutive-gap statistics. The contradiction establishes Lambda>=0 under the proof's analytic inputs; it does not turn finite tables into a proof of RH or identify a random-matrix process for H_t.
title: Heat flow turns spacing fluctuation into a dissipative obstruction

claim: An optimization can rank methods incorrectly when its objective or amortization regime differs from the certificate workload: a polynomial best for Landau's surrogate need not give the best finite zero-free constant, a precomputed fast method for many Z-values need not accelerate one Z-value, and an outer-first Gram-block search loses efficiency as block length changes.
historical_or_program_relation: These programs independently expose the same design obstruction at three levels—analytic surrogate, batch-versus-single evaluation, and within-block search order—and redirect optimization toward the downstream constant, query pattern, or empirical block type that actually controls cost.
limits: The three cost functions and algorithms have no common quantitative scale, so this is a shared failure mechanism rather than a transferable optimizer or performance theorem. Observed workload dependence does not show that the cited alternatives are globally optimal, and changing the objective must not weaken the mathematical certificate.
title: Computational improvements must optimize the actual proof workload

claim: Transform and residue calculus recast arithmetic data and zeros as additive terms of one explicit identity. Once the total geometric or discriminant-side quantity and the accessible prime-ideal contribution are computed, the otherwise difficult low-zero contribution can be recovered as the residual, turning a conceptual prime–zero duality into a practical measurement method.
historical_or_program_relation: Riemann's Euler-product/logarithm/Mellin-inversion route establishes why prime and zero data inhabit dual sides of an explicit formula; the discriminant computation exploits that exact decomposition when direct general Dedekind-zeta zero computation is unavailable.
limits: Subtraction recovers only the kernel-weighted aggregate appearing in the chosen identity, not individual zeros, their locations, or RH. Its validity depends on the explicit formula, kernel, truncation, and all other terms being correctly controlled, and cancellation can make the residual numerically sensitive.
title: An explicit formula can measure an inaccessible zero aggregate by subtraction

claim: Rigorous computation should export a height-bounded theorem, not a global trend: repeated logarithms can make divergent behavior appear bounded throughout feasible ranges, whereas an exact verified-height threshold can legitimately feed a separate theorem and yield an unconditional upper bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant.
historical_or_program_relation: The computational-history warning supplies the epistemic obstruction, early zero tables exemplify the correctly scoped finite RH claim, and the modern verification converts a much larger certified threshold into a different bounded analytic consequence without extrapolating the observed zero pattern.
limits: The slow-growth warning does not weaken a rigorously verified finite statement, and the threshold transfer proves only the stated Lambda bound, not RH or behavior above the verified height. Numerical persistence of a pattern, however extensive, cannot substitute for the theorem that maps a finite threshold to its downstream consequence.
title: Certified finite ranges support bounded transfers, not asymptotic extrapolation

claim: The two sources expose the same two-stage mechanism: the logarithmic derivative of the Euler product packages prime powers into analytic coefficients, nonvanishing on Re(s)=1 supplies the required boundary regularity apart from the pole at 1, and a Tauberian theorem transfers that behavior to asymptotics for Chebyshev's functions and hence prime counts.
historical_or_program_relation: The 2004 structural overview states the L-function template, while the 2026 historical account identifies Landau's Tauberian reorganization as the conceptual modularization of the 1896 Hadamard-de la Vallée Poussin route.
limits: This mechanism proves a prime number theorem from boundary nonvanishing, not RH or its square-root error term. The elementary Selberg-Erdős proof shows that this analytic factorization is not logically necessary, and analogous statements for broader L-function classes still require their own nonvanishing and transfer theorems.
title: The prime number theorem factors into boundary regularity and Tauberian transfer

claim: In the strengthened Nyman-Beurling construction, Mellin-Plancherel turns a damped fractional-part combination into a product of zeta, a partial Möbius Dirichlet approximation to 1/zeta, and a linear denominator. In the sequential Riesz criterion, a binomial transform of the samples 1/zeta(2j+2) produces c_k, and its exponential generating function is exactly e^x R(x)/x, preserving the decisive RH growth exponent between the sequence and Riesz's entire function.
historical_or_program_relation: These two Báez-Duarte-era programs replace direct zero location by discrete reciprocal-zeta data, but choose different representations to expose the needed convergence or cancellation.
limits: There is no stated transform from the Nyman-Beurling Hilbert norm to the c_k decay criterion, so the shared reciprocal-zeta ingredient does not make the two criteria equivalent to each other. The Mellin argument needs a separate domination theorem, while the binomial transform must include c_0 for genuine inversion and carries its own asymptotic exponent.
title: Mellin and binomial transforms discretize reciprocal zeta in inequivalent ways

claim: The closure criterion becomes zero exclusion because the Mellin transform of every fractional-part generator contains a zeta factor: at a putative zero with 1/2<Re(s)<1 the approximating span is annihilated, whereas the target indicator has nonzero Mellin value. Splitting the approximation error at one and using the tail coefficient identity makes this evaluation continuous along a norm-convergent sequence, yielding the contradiction.
historical_or_program_relation: The 2004 survey records the density equivalence as a change of problem; the 2021 treatment resolves the local proof mechanism that carries information from Hilbert closure back to the zero set.
limits: This is the zero-exclusion direction only. It presupposes actual Hilbert-norm approximation and the two separate controls on the bounded part and tail; it neither constructs the approximants nor supplies their convergence rate.
title: A hypothetical zero is an annihilator of the Nyman-Beurling dictionary but not its target

claim: A vanishing exponent on Möbius coefficients preserves the pointwise or fixed-coordinate target while making reciprocal-zeta tails estimable. Báez-Duarte upgrades this local regularization to Hilbert convergence by Mellin-Plancherel and an RH-dependent spectral majorant for the finite-sum limit, then uses functional symmetry unconditionally only to remove the auxiliary damping. Habsieger obtains the analogous fixed-coordinate and far-tail improvements, but the moving intermediate range still lacks a common square-summable dominator.
historical_or_program_relation: The later coordinate-space experiment isolates exactly which part of the earlier successful summability proof is not delivered merely by smoothing: global domination in the norm that defines the criterion.
limits: Pointwise or coordinatewise convergence is not norm convergence. The unconditional epsilon-removal step does not make Báez-Duarte's upstream construction unconditional, and the two papers use different bases and do not identify their approximants term by term.
title: Damping fixes local Möbius tails only when a global norm majorant is also supplied

claim: If f is the survival function of a positive random variable X, then expectation converts the random kernel into E[{X/t}]=-P f(t). Independently, after absolute convergence and boundary terms are certified, the same Müntz sum-integral operator P is represented as pseudo-convolution with the fractional-part discrepancy kernel. Random averaging therefore changes coordinates from a law of dilations to a deterministic convolutional closure object rather than merely smoothing noise.
historical_or_program_relation: The deterministic strong-kernel program supplies the operator identity and its convergence obligations; the probabilistic Nyman-Beurling program supplies a new source of kernels through survival laws.
limits: Both identities require their stated integrability, regularity, and interchange conditions. By themselves they establish neither Hilbert closure nor RH, and they do not identify every probabilistic criterion with the strong-kernel class.
title: Expected random fractional parts are a deterministic Müntz pseudo-convolution

claim: The deterministic criterion gains arithmetic discreteness by restricting the fractional-part dictionary to integer dilations, whose smallest scale decreases as the dictionary grows. The probabilistic lower bound makes that same resolution parameter explicit: after conditioning on admissible support, the random minimum m_n is inserted into the deterministic distance bound, giving D_n^2 bounded below on the scale 1/(log 2+E|log m_n|). Randomization therefore cannot bypass the need to reach sufficiently small dilations.
historical_or_program_relation: The probabilistic extension transports a deterministic geometric obstruction into a distribution-sensitive bound rather than treating random dictionaries as automatically richer.
limits: The result is a lower bound under the probabilistic support assumptions, not an upper bound or a convergence theorem. It does not make the deterministic and random spans equivalent, and a shrinking minimum alone is not sufficient for approximation.
title: The smallest available dilation is a geometric resolution bottleneck

claim: The Farey discrepancy criteria are carried by a precise representation chain: Möbius inversion removes the coprimality constraint, empirical-rank centering subtracts the deterministic triangular contribution from partial sums, and Bernoulli-Möbius coordinates plus cyclic Dedekind symmetrization convert the quadratic discrepancy into gcd-weighted correlations. Replacing the observed rank h(xi) by interval length loses a residue-class fluctuation that available cancellation identities do not control.
historical_or_program_relation: The 2004 list of L1 and L2 Farey equivalents is unpacked by the 1996 source into the combinatorial transform, centering choice, and correlation identity on which those geometric formulations depend.
limits: The absolute- and squared-discrepancy criteria remain different estimates even though both concern Farey ranks. The obstruction to naive centering is local to the stated statistics, and the cyclotomic-height criterion listed beside Farey discrepancy is a separate translation with no bridge established here.
title: Farey RH criteria depend on Möbius removal of coprimality and exact empirical centering

claim: The harmonic-number expression is not merely a cosmetic removal of Euler's constant: it is bounded above Robin's main term for the RH direction and within O(n/log n) of that term for the converse. Under RH, Robin's universal tail bound plus computation of the finite prefix proves the inequality; under RH failure, an off-line zero yields infinitely many excesses of order n log log n/(log n)^beta with beta<1/2, which eventually outrun the harmonic-envelope error.
historical_or_program_relation: Robin's 1984 arithmetic criterion is converted in 2002 into an all-integer, undefined-constant-free statement, and the 2026 survey places that conversion beside other representation changes such as density and coefficient positivity.
limits: The final statement is elementary but its equivalence imports Robin's non-elementary theorems. The finite computation closes only the explicitly bounded prefix after the asymptotic proof, and the criterion does not by itself suggest how to establish Robin's universal inequality.
title: Lagarias's elementary statement works by a rate-compatible envelope around Robin's criterion

claim: Primorial and colossally abundant constructions package many small-prime factors into extremal multiplicative observables, so an RH-equivalent one-sided inequality depends on how prime-counting fluctuations perturb the product, not merely on its limiting scale. The primorial Dedekind-psi ratio approaching e^gamma/zeta(2) supplies neither the sign nor the rate needed to dominate the explicit Euler-tail surplus; a normalized ratio may approach one from below with a larger deficit.
historical_or_program_relation: Lagarias explains why smooth small-prime products act as amplifiers of prime irregularity, while the 2023 Nicolas-based preprint provides a concrete failed limit argument that omits the effective one-sided comparison such amplification requires.
limits: This diagnoses a proof gap in the preprint, not a counterexample to the Nicolas criterion or to RH. Nicolas's prime-product criterion and Robin-Lagarias divisor criteria are distinct, and Lagarias's amplifier discussion does not furnish the missing estimate for the primorial Dedekind-psi ratio.
title: Extremal prime products preserve the sign-and-rate information that bare limits discard

claim: Completion symmetry can be spent as a local proof module: it turns Báez-Duarte's reflected zeta quotient into an unconditional vertical-strip majorant for removing damping, and together with Hadamard and gamma asymptotics it orients F'/F on remote contours for comparative zero counts. The completed Eisenstein series simultaneously shows that spectral reflection s to 1-s is independent of modular symmetry in z; the coexistence of these identifications alone supplies no critical-line zero theorem.
historical_or_program_relation: Across automorphic, approximation, and Speiser-style programs, functional equations repeatedly reduce a hard two-sided analysis to one controlled side, while later counterexamples and failed analogues sharpen the boundary between transport and zero-location conclusions.
limits: The functions and hypotheses are different, so no theorem is transferred among the three programs. Báez-Duarte's local limit removal occurs after an RH-dependent construction, and the Hurwitz/Lerch observations are computational nonconfirmation rather than a classification theorem.
title: Functional symmetry transports estimates but is not a critical-line certificate

claim: In the Lagarias criterion, analytic inequalities settle every n beyond an explicit threshold, so checking 1<=n<=5040 closes a genuinely finite residual obligation. For the Báez-Duarte sequence, an off-critical zero can have a height-suppressed coefficient whose eventual power growth appears only at an enormous index, so a long finite run showing k^(-3/4)-scale behavior does not bound the unchecked tail.
historical_or_program_relation: The contrast separates proof-completing computation from exploratory verification: both inspect finite arithmetic data, but only the former is backed by an analytic cutoff theorem.
limits: The delayed-crossover discussion for c_k is heuristic and assumes the relevant explicit zero expansion, including simplicity in the stated formula. It supplies no numerical cutoff and does not compare the computational cost of the two criteria.
title: Finite computation is decisive only after analysis proves that the unchecked region is finite

claim: For central zeta coefficients, saddle-point ratio expansions force normalized Jensen polynomials of each fixed degree toward Hermite polynomials and hence eventual hyperbolicity, while RH requires hyperbolicity for every degree and every shift. In the sequential Riesz criterion, the observed bulk is likewise dominated by low critical-line zeros, while a remote off-line zero may affect only an unbounded later range. Both representations can therefore stabilize on every tested local regime without discharging the global quantifier.
historical_or_program_relation: The 2008 sequence experiment and the 2019 Jensen-polynomial theorem turn an informal warning about finite evidence into two representation-specific mechanisms: spectral coefficient suppression in one case and fixed-degree universality in the other.
limits: There is no quantitative map between a Jensen threshold and a c_k crossover. The delayed off-line contribution is heuristic in the cited sequence analysis, and fixed-degree eventual Jensen hyperbolicity leaves low shifts and degrees growing with the shift outside its conclusion.
title: Stable asymptotic bulk behavior can coexist with an unresolved universal RH quantifier

claim: Riemann's prime-counting formula already required the zero terms to be ordered by magnitude because rearrangement can change the value; the later Delsarte-Weil formulation relocates the same prime-zero duality into a distribution evaluated on test functions, where the summation convention, contour decay, and admissible function class become explicit parts of the interface.
historical_or_program_relation: The proof burden changes from interpreting one conditionally ordered explicit sum to proving a distributional identity and then establishing a uniform positivity property on a controlled class of tests.
limits: The distributional reformulation does not make every raw zero sum absolutely convergent and does not supply Weil positivity or prove RH. The two units support a representation change, not a claim that the later formalism was derived specifically to repair the quoted ordering warning.
title: From a conditionally ordered zero sum to a distributional test-function interface

claim: Hardy's Fourier-and-moment sign argument forces infinitely many critical-line zeros but does not exhaust the zeros below a height; Hutchinson and Lehmer closed that gap by matching critical-line sign changes to a global zero count, and the modern count-only design preserves this completeness logic while declining to refine each ordinate beyond what counting needs.
historical_or_program_relation: The computational burden moved from producing critical-line existence witnesses, to proving equality between witness and total counts, to minimizing precision and storage without weakening that count equality.
limits: Every computational conclusion remains bounded by its certified height. Sign changes alone can miss even-multiplicity zeros, while a total count alone does not locate zeros on the line; the certificate depends on composing both sides with controlled numerical error.
title: Critical-line witnesses became finite-range certificates only after global counting

claim: The Gram test supplied cheap critical-line intervals, but empty intervals were compensated by extra zeros nearby and failures clustered; Lehmer therefore used an explicit remainder bound to route ambiguous or failed intervals to subdivision and a sharper formula, while modern verification stops refining a zero as soon as a rigorous sign-change count is secured.
historical_or_program_relation: A presumed one-zero-per-cell rule was replaced by bounded-error screening plus targeted fallback, and later by a certificate objective that spends precision on completeness rather than on uniformly accurate ordinates.
limits: The modern count-only unit does not claim to reuse Lehmer's exact Gram-point screening algorithm. Local compensation patterns are empirical failure taxonomy, not a theorem that every future Gram failure is nearby, so an independent global count remains necessary.
title: Failures of Gram's local rule forced an exception-driven audit architecture

claim: The 1990 certificate searched for a nonreal zero of a Jensen polynomial for a chosen heat parameter, but its required degree and precision exploded as the parameter approached zero; the 1993 Lehmer-pair certificate instead used a consecutive pair of zeros of H0 whose squared gap is small relative to a rigorously bounded inverse-square interaction with all other zeros.
historical_or_program_relation: The lower-bound program changed its witness from high-degree global root geometry under heat deformation to a local close pair normalized by a global interaction term, making a spectacular small gap useful only after the surrounding-zero burden was certified.
limits: A close gap by itself is not a Lehmer certificate, and the pair method still requires consecutiveness and tail bounds over all other zeros. Both methods yield lower bounds for Lambda; neither supplies the RH-equivalent upper bound Lambda <= 0.
title: The de Bruijn-Newman lower-bound witness shifted from a global polynomial to a normalized zero pair

claim: The 1994 route would force Lambda >= 0 from an infinite family of certified Lehmer pairs with vanishing gaps, whereas the 2020 route assumes Lambda < 0, derives that almost all heat-flow zeros must approach a local lattice, and contradicts the known positive proportion of zeta gaps strictly below mean spacing.
historical_or_program_relation: The decisive witness changed from locating infinitely many exceptional close pairs one by one to proving that the negative-Lambda dynamics would suppress a population-level spacing fluctuation that is already known to occur.
limits: The two arguments use different gap hypotheses and are not interchangeable: an arbitrary small gap need not be a Lehmer pair, and the Rodgers-Tao contradiction uses the consequences of the assumption Lambda < 0 together with external spacing results. Lambda >= 0 alone does not prove RH.
title: Newman's lower bound escaped the search for exceptional pairs through gap distribution

claim: The classical numerical certificate compares the total zero count with critical-line sign changes to prove RH only below a height H; the 2021 computation reuses such an exact height as an input to a separate heat-flow theorem, where exceeding 2.51e12 yields the unconditional upper bound Lambda <= 0.2.
historical_or_program_relation: Finite verification acquired a second role: besides enlarging the checked RH range, its precise endpoint now discharges a threshold assumption in a global de Bruijn-Newman estimate.
limits: The transfer gives only the stated upper bound on Lambda, not Lambda <= 0 or RH, and its numerical value depends on the external threshold table. Selected high zeros or an uncertified record count would not satisfy the required finite-height premise.
title: A finite RH certificate became an input threshold for a heat-flow bound

claim: The 1936 higher-genus program replaced elliptic endomorphisms by self-correspondences but still lacked a theory of differentials and a norm generalization leading to positive definiteness; the mature finite-field picture forces the equivalent sign through an intersection-form index theorem, while the classical problem still lacks corresponding cohomology, Frobenius, and an index theorem.

limits: Hasse's missing norm step is not identified with the later classical missing index theorem, and the units do not establish a transfer from finite-field divisors to classical test functions. Bombieri also notes that Maass L-functions may have no guiding algebraic-geometric model.
title: Correspondences exposed a positivity mechanism and the geometry still missing classically

claim: Semi-local scaling operators canonically reproduce finite local terms of the explicit formula, but the proposed Hardy-space proof fails because local-factor ratios can have unit modulus on the critical line without being bounded, and the resulting sign inequality is false; the authors identify the omitted global Poisson normalization as essential, in contrast with the finite-field setting where an intersection theorem forces the sign.
historical_or_program_relation: The analytic program narrowed its obstruction from constructing relevant operators to controlling principal-value normalizations globally enough to prove Weil positivity, while geometry remains the comparison case in which the required sign has a structural source.
limits: Failure of this inner-function inequality does not refute Weil positivity or all operator-theoretic approaches. The finite-field intersection form is only a comparison mechanism here; no map to the semi-local Hilbert spaces or a classical index theorem is supplied.
title: Canonical local terms did not remove the global normalization burden in Weil positivity

claim: Hilbert-Polya requires a natural Hermitian operator whose eigenvalues are the zero ordinates, whereas the Veneziano construction supplies an equivalent integral identity and only conjectures an effective Riemann string; independently, a quantum-state overlap can approximate zeta accurately even when its Hamiltonian fails termwise to approximate the intended logarithmic spectrum.
historical_or_program_relation: These later physical representations shift attention from spectral realization to amplitude, phase, or aggregate overlap, but thereby expose a stricter proof burden: reproducing a function-level observable is not the same as realizing its nontrivial zeros as a self-adjoint spectrum.
limits: The string amplitude and Jaynes-Cummings overlap are distinct models and are not evidence against each other. Neither an equivalent RH criterion nor aggregate numerical agreement constructs the required operator, proves self-adjointness, or forces zero ordinates to be real eigenvalues.
title: Physical reformulations preserve zeta data without meeting the Hilbert-Polya burden

claim: The self-adjoint prolate extension has a discrete negative spectrum with the same ultraviolet behavior as squared zeta-zero ordinates and is interpreted as capturing the archimedean contribution, but a finite RH certificate separately needs an exhaustive total-zero count and equally many critical-line witnesses.
historical_or_program_relation: The spectral program can match the leading high-energy counting architecture before it has identified the individual zeta spectrum; the older certification logic makes precise why matching density or asymptotics alone leaves the location burden untouched.
limits: The prolate unit claims ultraviolet similarity, not equality of spectra, and explicitly narrows the interpretation to an archimedean contribution. The finite certificate is bounded-height and does not prove that no future refinement of the prolate model could recover more information.
title: Ultraviolet spectral agreement captures a counting scale, not critical-line location

claim: Voronin universality approximates nonvanishing holomorphic targets on compact subsets of 1/2 < Re(s) < 1 by vertical zeta shifts, while Borchsenius-Jessen shows that every nonzero value x is assumed infinitely often arbitrarily close to the critical line from the right; together they isolate zero alignment as a property not preserved by generic value-distribution flexibility.
historical_or_program_relation: The almost-periodic and universality programs reveal enormous orbit density, but the proof burden for RH remains tied to the exceptional target value zero rather than to approximation of generic nonzero functions or values.
limits: The universality theorem and the a-point theorem have different quantifiers and regions, and neither is derived from the other in these units. Uniform approximation on compacta does not determine the global zero set, and the off-line solutions of zeta(s)=x for x != 0 do not imply an off-line zero of zeta.
title: Universality's flexible approximation stops exactly at the exceptional zero value

claim: Lehmer proposed targeting immense heights where early and late Riemann-Siegel terms nearly cancel, but later computational history warns that repeated-logarithm effects can remain invisible on every feasible range; a 2024 zero-free-region bootstrap now requires rigorous exclusion of zeros in 355 prescribed boxes at heights from about exp(40000) to exp(5e7), beyond current raw computation and zero-density estimates.
historical_or_program_relation: The numerical burden changed from searching selectively for a possible counterexample-like witness to certifying absence uniformly in tiny, predetermined high-altitude regions needed to close an analytic induction.
limits: Slow asymptotic visibility does not prove that computation can never reach a useful regime, and Lehmer's cancellation heuristic does not target the 2024 boxes. The envelope construction is conditional future work, not an achieved zero-free region or an RH proof.
title: High-altitude computation changed from targeted witness search to an exclusion bottleneck

claim: After arithmetic factors were scaled out, characteristic-polynomial moments predicted the previously missing constants in zeta moments; the later analogy audit separates leading ensemble agreement, arithmetic corrections, and deterministic unitary polynomials that can violate the zeta-side expectation despite having all zeros on the unit circle.
historical_or_program_relation: The program advanced from empirical zero-spacing analogy to quantitative moment prediction, while its validation burden became explicit: choose the correct random ensemble, restore arithmetic factors, and control whether deterministic counterexamples are statistically negligible at the matched scale.
limits: The zeta moment formulas remain conjectural in the stated generality, and rarity under Haar measure is not a deterministic theorem about zeta. Statistical success does not construct a Hilbert-Polya operator, force RH, or transfer every property of unitary polynomials.
title: Random matrices predicted missing moment constants but only at a statistical interface

claim: Bombieri argues that zeta is a prototype and that functional equations and Euler products often come from modular parametrization or simultaneous Laplacian-Hecke eigenstructure, with establishing those sources already difficult; the Selberg class abstracts the shared analytic package and primitive factorization, but leaves the tasks of proving its members arithmetic and proving prime-coefficient orthogonality or a prime number theorem.
historical_or_program_relation: Enlarging the problem exposes reusable structure, yet transfers the proof burden from analyzing zeta in isolation to recognizing which analytic objects genuinely arise arithmetically and controlling their primitive interactions.
limits: Selberg-class axioms do not prove that every member is arithmetic, do not supply the conjectured orthogonality, and do not imply RH. The abstraction also does not resolve Bombieri's warning that some Maass L-functions lack a direct geometric origin.
title: Generalizing zeta moved the obstruction from one function to class membership and orthogonality

claim: In the de Branges route, xi supplies several required entire-function and monotonicity features but the decisive shifted-inner-product positivity condition is false; in the semi-local Hardy route, local-factor ratios have unit modulus on the critical line but fail boundedness and the proposed sign inequality is false.
historical_or_program_relation: Both episodes isolate the same proof-design error at different analytic interfaces: attractive symmetry or boundary behavior does not automatically extend to the global positivity/boundedness needed to force zero location.
limits: The de Branges space condition and the local-factor Hardy condition concern different functions, spaces, and inequalities, so this is a shared obstruction pattern rather than one counterexample or theorem. Neither failure rules out other Hilbert-space or positivity formulations of RH.
title: Two Hilbert-space routes failed at the extra global property their boundary structure suggested

claim: The abstract two-sided L-function package has a concrete modular realization: simultaneous Hecke eigenvectors make Fourier coefficients multiplicative and hence produce Euler factors, while the Mellin completion transports modular transformation symmetry into a functional equation. The two analytic features are therefore outputs of two compatible structures on the same eigenform, not unrelated axioms.
historical_or_program_relation: This construction-level account sharpens the program in which zeta is treated as a prototype and the wider L-function class is studied to expose the arithmetic or geometric source of its analytic package.
limits: Hecke diagonalization applies to the stated modular setting; it neither gives a modular origin for classical zeta nor proves that every axiomatically admissible L-function is automorphic. An Euler product plus functional equation does not force critical-line zeros.
title: Hecke selection concretely couples Euler factors to modular functional symmetry

claim: For a nonreal Dirichlet character, multiplying the completed L-functions of χ and its conjugate makes the reflection internal to one analytic object without changing the union of their zeros. By contrast, orthogonal or symplectic type is a pairing sign transported through motivic, ℓ-adic, and automorphic realizations and can obstruct criticality at the center. Thus self-functional-equation form and representation-theoretic self-duality carry different information.
historical_or_program_relation: The Dirichlet-family extension shows how GRH survives dual pairing, while the later motivic program refines the word self-dual into a sign invariant with arithmetic consequences.
limits: The product L(s,χ)L(s,χ̄) changes degree and does not turn either factor into a geometric object. The pairing-sign argument uses the stated regularity and algebraicity assumptions and a conjectural motivic bridge; neither construction proves GRH or transfers a conclusion to ζ.
title: Analytic self-duality can be manufactured, while geometric pairing sign cannot

claim: Low-zero behavior in an L-function family must be decomposed before assigning a symmetry type: persistent central zeros are removed as a rank contribution, root numbers split symplectic families into parity subfamilies, and a parity-sensitive off-diagonal prime–Kloosterman term distinguishes SO(even) from SO(odd) even when the diagonal does not.
historical_or_program_relation: This refines random-matrix family classification from a single bulk label into independent arithmetic mechanisms for central mass, functional-equation sign, and the first symmetry-sensitive density correction.
limits: These are family-level low-zero statistics, not statements about every member or about classical ζ. The cited off-diagonal calculation uses its own support range and GRH input for Dirichlet L-functions; rank, root-number balance, and bulk type cannot be inferred from one another.
title: Persistent rank, root-number parity, and bulk symmetry are separate channels

claim: Petersson weighting is what turns a cusp-form average of Hecke coefficients into a diagonal plus a controlled Kloosterman–Bessel off-diagonal, but the same weighting defines a different probability measure from unweighted counting. When the weight is itself a fluctuating central L-value, weighted low-zero density can display a symmetry signature inconsistent with the representation-theoretic type of the unweighted family.
historical_or_program_relation: A standard analytic access mechanism becomes an estimand audit: the trace formula supplies the family average, and later symmetry work identifies removal of its natural weights as an additional proof obligation.
limits: This does not invalidate the exact weighted Petersson identities or show that every harmonic weight changes symmetry. The two cited families and weight normalizations are not identical; an unweighted conclusion requires a separate weight-removal argument.
title: Trace-formula diagonalization may change the family measure

claim: Trace-formula family statistics depend on a main term carried by the identity orbit: in positive-volume harmonic families it becomes Plancherel mass, analogous to the Petersson diagonal that normalizes Hecke averages. Imposing a Plancherel-null local condition deletes that leading mass, so ordinary limit-multiplicity machinery cannot isolate the desired subfamily before any zero-symmetry test begins.
historical_or_program_relation: The mechanism marks a boundary in the automorphic-family program: increasingly arithmetic or cohomological local restrictions may make the natural trace tool lose its counting baseline.
limits: Petersson's GL(2) formula and the general Arthur-trace setting are examples of the same signal/error architecture, not the same theorem. Failure of the main term does not imply that the constrained family is empty or that its symmetry conjecture is false; it identifies a method bottleneck.
title: A zero-mass local condition removes the trace formula's main counting signal

claim: In the finite-field model, intersecting a graph with the diagonal becomes an alternating cohomological trace because the diagonal is the identity kernel. Classical explicit formulas instead use ζ'/ζ, contour residues, and Fourier test functions to turn prime powers and zeros into dual distributions; Lefschetz-style kernel restriction explains why a fixed-point formula has trace coefficients but does not identify the classical arithmetic distribution with a Frobenius trace.

limits: The finite-field equality has an actual variety, map, and Weil cohomology; the classical formula is an analytic distributional identity. No graph, cohomology group, or Frobenius operator for ζ follows from their formal resemblance, and a trace identity alone supplies no positivity or RH.
title: Geometric and classical trace formulas linearize different objects

claim: The historical move from elliptic endomorphisms to higher-genus self-correspondences constructed the algebraic carrier but left the norm or positive-definite form missing. Weil forms later isolate the needed positive-adjoint interface on algebraic correspondences, and the finite-field index theorem turns the corresponding sign into zero-location control; the classical explicit-formula criterion likewise exposes a uniform sign as the unfilled burden.
historical_or_program_relation: The sequence separates discovery of the right operators from discovery of the form that constrains their spectrum, explaining why correspondence algebra alone did not complete the positive-characteristic proof program.
limits: Weil-form positivity, surface-intersection negativity, and the classical test-function quadratic form are related proof roles, not identified forms. Their domains and sign conventions differ, and the finite-field mechanism does not provide the missing classical correspondence or prove ζ-RH.
title: Correspondences become a zero-location mechanism only after a positive adjoint is supplied

claim: Both curve zeta functions and classical completed zeta expose reciprocal zero symmetry, but only the finite-field setting compresses all extension-field point counts into a rational generating function with finitely many Frobenius inverse roots. There the functional equation pairs reciprocal roots and upgrades a one-sided radius bound to exact modulus q^(1/2); classical completion makes the involution visible without supplying a finite point-count spectrum.
historical_or_program_relation: The solved function-field analogue clarifies which extra representation—not merely the shared functional equation—makes its RH accessible.
limits: q^(1/2)-modulus is a function-field weight statement, not the classical line Re(s)=1/2 under a literal change of variables. Classical ζ has no source-supported Frobenius action or finite rational numerator here, so the finite-field proof cannot be transferred by analogy alone.
title: Finite-field functional symmetry acts on a finite Frobenius spectrum

claim: For a Hecke eigenform, a period integral packages finitely many critical L-values as coefficients of a reciprocal polynomial. In the large-weight proof, a zero-transparent exponential model supplies monotone boundary phase and a separate uniform error bound transfers its sign changes to unit-circle roots. This is a finite coefficient-encoding theorem whose symmetry ultimately comes from the modular functional equation.
historical_or_program_relation: The construction is a genuine modular descendant of the L-function package, but it relocates the zero problem from the analytic L-function to an auxiliary polynomial where phase and perturbation estimates are available.
limits: The circle zeros are zeros of the period polynomial, not zeros of L(f,s), and they imply neither GRH for the modular L-function nor RH for classical ζ. The argument needs its stated weight/level regime and error inequality; reciprocal symmetry alone does not force circle roots.
title: Period-polynomial circle roots concern an encoding of critical modular L-values

claim: A symmetry-preserving integral transform sends x↦1−x invariance to a polynomial functional equation s↦1−s, so recentering makes its critical-line claim a real-rootedness problem just as completion and s=1/2+it do for ξ. The proof then uses a finite recurrence, continuity in a parameter, interlacing, and exclusion of common-root collisions through a cubic characteristic equation.
historical_or_program_relation: The example isolates how reflection symmetry can be combined with an independent finite-dimensional root-control mechanism, offering an analogue of the formulation rather than a route to the classical conjecture.
limits: These transformed polynomials have finite degree and a recurrence/interlacing structure absent from the cited classical ξ formulation. Their functional equation has no demonstrated Euler product, prime explicit formula, or ζ-divisor content; their real-rootedness does not imply classical RH.
title: A polynomial critical-line analogue is proved by finite recurrence geometry

claim: The zero-density argument first reflects an overlong expression through the functional equation into a dual finite sum plus remainder, then combines correlation control with fourth moments; powering a zero-detecting polynomial moves its witness into the admissible length regime of that large-value theorem. A mollifier uses a complementary design—approximate inversion and an exact low-range coefficient gap—to place L-times-mollifier inside an averaged norm estimate.
historical_or_program_relation: Across Dirichlet L-function methods, finite polynomials are engineered interfaces between zeros or near-inversion and the scale at which family mean values are actually controllable.
limits: Powering a zero detector and multiplying by a mollifier are not interchangeable: one transfers zero witnesses to density bounds, the other suppresses coefficients on average. Neither proves a zero-free half-plane or GRH, and the OCR-damaged zero-density span does not support exact lengths, exponents, or thresholds beyond the qualitative assembly.
title: Dirichlet-polynomial proofs succeed by matching witnesses to mean-value inputs

claim: Placing L-functions in a conductor- or parameter-varying family changes the target from locating every zero of one function to estimating a population observable. In quadratic families this lets large-sieve or density tools prove nonvanishing and rank information, or rule out the scenario that every sufficiently large member has an exceptional real zero, without resolving each member separately.
historical_or_program_relation: This is a deliberate weakening that turns otherwise inaccessible individual questions into average theorems while preserving central-point and low-zero information that high-zero universality can forget.
limits: There is no formal universal notion of family in the number-field setting, and conclusions depend on the chosen parametrization, conductor ordering, and measure. Positive proportions or average rank bounds do not prove GRH for any unspecified member and say nothing directly about classical ζ.
title: Family formation trades individual control for deformable statistical leverage

claim: Automorphic trace formulas push local Plancherel measure through an L-map to obtain Satake-parameter statistics, retaining a local representation-theoretic origin for Euler factors. Characteristic-polynomial models instead retain symmetry type and conductor-scaled zero density to predict universal moment structure, while leaving the prime-local Euler product to a separate arithmetic factor.
historical_or_program_relation: The comparison gives a staged family program: derive local parameter laws from spectral counting, then test which aggregate zero or value statistics depend only on symmetry and which still remember Euler arithmetic.
limits: A Plancherel pushforward is not a derivation of random-matrix moment conjectures, and the matrix model does not reconstruct Satake parameters or Euler factors. The cited moment comparisons concern primitive families and provide conjectural or numerical calibration, not individual RH or a classification of ζ.
title: Two statistical abstractions preserve symmetry while discarding different arithmetic data

claim: The explicit formula is an exact trace-like bridge: test functions turn the logarithmic derivative into dual prime-power and zero distributions. Its usefulness for RH begins only when an additional sign or spectral constraint forces location; family positivity is presently operational, while random-matrix spacing and finite-field cohomology identify plausible structural obligations but do not supply the missing classical operator or index theorem.
historical_or_program_relation: The trace and random-matrix programs refine the classical explicit formula from an encoding into a search for the extra positivity, self-adjointness, or geometry that would make the encoding restrictive.
limits: Matching spectral statistics is not construction of a Hilbert–Pólya operator, and a proposed spectral representation is not useful solely because its trace resembles the explicit formula. Finite-field geometry is an analogue, family positivity gives separate average results, and none of these observations proves ζ-RH.
title: Prime–zero trace encoding does not itself force zero location

claim: In both finite-field and automorphic settings, a positive-coefficient auxiliary Dirichlet series prevents cancellation at its convergence boundary. Landau's theorem can then turn the location of a global singularity into one-sided bounds on local Euler-factor roots; Rankin–Selberg constructions make that positivity structural by converting local power sums into nonnegative quadratic coefficients.
historical_or_program_relation: The shared mechanism shows how global analytic continuation can control local spectra only after passing to a positivity-preserving auxiliary L-function, complementing geometric weight arguments.
limits: The auxiliary series, convergence boundary, and local parameters differ between the two settings. Landau positivity yields one-sided local bounds under its hypotheses, not critical-line zero location, purity by itself, or RH for classical ζ.
title: Coefficient positivity lets a global boundary constrain every local Euler root

claim: The squared-modulus short-window integral is a positive coarse-graining of the local zeta landscape: its known global mean can coexist with a different typical scale if rare windows dominate, while the beta-dependent free-energy response tests that domination across a family of exponents rather than at one mean value.
historical_or_program_relation: The freezing program supplies a distributional response-curve conjecture for the same kind of local partition mass whose typical size is isolated as an analytic question in the short-window second-moment program.
limits: The short-window source does not establish a mean/typical gap or a tail mechanism. The reported freezing plateau is numerical, uses lower-order arithmetic renormalization, and is explicitly a proposed model rather than a theorem for zeta.
title: A partition observable separates its mean from its typical and frozen regimes

claim: Both maximum programs replace pointwise search by a path through prime scales, but in opposite directions: Cauchy localization, smooth-factor thresholds, and optimized high moments make upper-barrier failure rare, whereas matched-variance prime blocks, a spatial grid, and Paley-Zygmund produce a point whose blocks are simultaneously high.
historical_or_program_relation: Together the programs decompose a local-maximum problem into an analytic transfer to prime blocks and a probability problem on correlated multiscale paths, with barrier estimates for the upper direction and second-moment abundance for the lower direction.
limits: The arguments use different approximations, events, parameter ranges, and inequality directions. They do not identify an exact common random field, prove the FHK limiting law, or convert the typical-window lower bound into a global-maximum result.
title: Upper and lower maximum bounds use opposite sides of multiscale path geometry

claim: A smooth/rough factorization of a shortened approximate-functional-equation polynomial preserves zeta only in a quantified mean-square sense, while the smoothed hybrid Euler-Hadamard factorization moves mass between prime and nearby-zero factors as its cutoff changes while preserving their product. In both cases the cutoff is part of the representation and records what the separated factors forget.

limits: The smooth/rough factors are finite Dirichlet polynomials with an L2 error and are not the hybrid prime and zero factors. The cutoff-compensation evidence includes a representation-sensitivity visualization and does not justify termwise identification or statistical independence of either pair.
title: Two cutoff factorizations preserve different invariants

claim: The GCD quadratic form designs coefficients with many favorable multiplicative ratios, while the positive Dirichlet-series lemma and compact-frequency kernel convert approximate relations of the form km approximately n into a localized lower bound. Thus multiplicative-ratio geometry is the interface between arithmetic support optimization and analytic amplification.

limits: The GCD construction and the positive-convolution theorem have distinct support, smoothing, and interval budgets. Their combination does not prove an optimal zeta maximum, transfer the GCD constant automatically, or apply when the projected Dirichlet coefficients have uncontrolled signs.
title: GCD optimization and positive convolution separate resonator design from analytic transfer

Positivity can no longer certify that discarding terms improves a one-sided lower bound.

limits: This is a method-specific obstruction, not an impossibility theorem for extreme values of S or S1. The zero correction and conditional assumptions must remain explicit, and an absolute-value conclusion for S cannot be promoted to a one-sided conclusion for S1.
title: Signed projections obstruct the monotone GCD-resonance route

A finite cutoff is separately required when a boundedly convergent Voronoi series meets an improper integral.

limits: The auxiliary functions, domains, and boundary operations are different, so this is not a common theorem. Analytic continuation does not supply a probabilistic meaning at nonpositive drift, and it does not by itself license termwise integration or remove the mean-square convergence boundary.
title: Continuation before specialization keeps boundary claims auditable

Expanding higher critical-line moments instead exposes shifted additive divisor correlations, and longer polynomials reveal distinct rational-direction strata that can contribute main terms rather than errors.

limits: The second-moment truncation and saddle machinery do not estimate the higher shifted correlations. The random-matrix or swap recipe is a target for the divisor program, not a theorem imported into it, and the rational strata do not establish the full zeta-moment conjecture without analytic error control.
title: Higher moments replace a controlled divisor oscillation by stratified divisor correlations

The mean-square proof repairs an invalid infinite sum-improper integral exchange by cutting the integral before substitution, while a long Dirichlet polynomial reproduces the second moment only after a functional-equation Fourier identity accounts for off-diagonal mass; negative predictions for higher moments then falsify a heuristic missing correlation classes.

limits: The repairs address different analytic failures. Nonnegativity detects that the higher-moment heuristic is incomplete but does not identify or prove the missing terms, and the verified second-moment Fourier identity does not validate the corresponding higher-moment extrapolation.
title: Cutoffs, Fourier identities, and nonnegativity audit formal moment expansions

claim: Past their diagonal ranges, both zero-pair statistics and zeta moments reduce analytic questions to translation correlations of arithmetic coefficients: pair correlation asks for shifted von Mangoldt products Lambda(n)Lambda(n+h), while the sixth-moment route asks for shifted correlations of divisor coefficients arising from zeta cubed.

limits: Von Mangoldt and divisor correlations have different weights, shift ranges, smoothing, and conjectural inputs. Hardy-Littlewood averaging, random-matrix agreement, or a delta-method recipe in one setting cannot be imported as a theorem in the other.
title: Zero statistics and higher moments meet different shifted arithmetic correlations
